messages:
jess: quick q — trying to finalize tooltip copy for the console that explains why autofallback sampled a request. want to avoid operator panic when they see 'fell back: policy 7' :sweat_smile:
omar: +1 on not alarming. what are the fields we can surface safely? policy_id, sample_rate, reason_code?
jess: thinking: show a one‑line reason like 'latency spike' or 'error-class: downstream-500', then a small detail link to full audit. default should be non-technical for PMs.
maya: agree. maybe show an abbreviated trace: "latency>1200ms -> model-quantized fallback". keep it human: "Slow model response, routed to fallback model".
kevin: telemetry constraint: we sample only 1/100 by default for payloads to control cost. if tooltip links to audit we need stable id to find the full event even if payload not stored. audit should store meta: sample_seed + policy_id + shard_ts.
omar: good point. if we always write a tiny audit row for every fallback (no payload) we can keep retention short (7d) and still let operators click through to partial context.
jess: UX question: show "why" inline or only on hover/click? ops like inline because fast triage, but product folks want less clutter.
maya: compromise: inline short label + tooltip with one-line rationale + CTA "view event" that opens audit panel. default collapsed on mobile.
kevin: backend: adding a small audit row per fallback increases QPS on the audit writer. could we flush to a separate low-TPS table with TTL? that table only keeps meta (policy_id, reason_code, sample_seed, route, latency_ms, model_variant). size estimate: 10M fallbacks/day -> 10 fields * 10 bytes ~= 100MB/day. ok-ish but still a cost.
jess: we need a product decision — do we: A) show inline short reason and write meta for every fallback, or B) only write meta for sampled fallbacks and show "sampled fallback" in UI with a link that may be empty?
omar: Ops will hate B. they need deterministic traces for incidents. leaning A.
maya: +1 for A but make sampling tunable by org. default A for enterprise accounts, B for self-serve.
kevin: technical nit: if we write meta for every fallback, we must ensure unique audit key so console can always fetch the event even if payload removed. propose key format: audit:{org}:{ts}:{policy_id}:{seed}.
omar: add note: include anonymized routing decision snapshot (only flags, thresholds, no user prompt text) to keep PII out.
jess: example tooltip copy draft: "Why this request fell back: Slow primary model response. Click to view audit details (no user text stored)." thoughts?
maya: short and clear. add an expandable line: "Operator actions: retry / pin primary model / open rollback"
kevin: implementer note for UI: when user clicks "view audit" we hit /audit/events?key=audit:{org}:{ts}:... which returns JSON like:\n```\n{\n  "policy_id": "policy-7",\n  "reason_code": "latency-spike",\n  "latency_ms": "1340",\n  "sample_seed": "0xdeadbeef",\n  "model_stack": "m-v1 -> m-v1-quant",\n  "decision_flags": "cache-miss,kv-expire"\n}\n```\nkevin: (this is config preview only, we won't return request prompts)
omar: small UX ask: show "sample seed" only to engineers (collapse for product/pm role). we can surface "debug id" to everyone.
jess: agreed. make the label "debug id" in UI and show seed in advanced view.
maya: one more: add a tiny CTA inside tooltip: "why this policy triggered?" -> opens human-friendly explanation with thresholds (e.g., latency>1s for 3s window). that will cut down on pings to infra.
kevin: backend will need to return trigger snapshot with threshold explanation. we can generate that from the policy engine (already has readable rule text).
omar: ops-bot: recorded incident pattern: when fallback shows without explanation we get paging. better doc + in-UI rationale reduced pages by ~40% in the last trial. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident-bot: note logged: trial reduced wakeups by 38% (2025-09-11 -> 2025-09-18).
jess: next steps: kevin to spec audit row shape + retention defaults; omar to spec UI affordance (inline short text + clickthrough); maya to write tooltip copy variations; i'll coordinate rollout flags and A/B test.
kevin: will send PR w/ schema and perf numbers by EOD Friday.
omar: i'll sketch the console mock showing collapsed vs inline and send to #design.
maya: I'll prep copy deck and examples for product.
jess: thanks all — let's try to keep the initial rollout non-disruptive. if anyone thinks sampling-only default is required for cost reasons, ping me before Friday. :pray:
